newsitem.title: USA: Both sides rest cases in O.J. Simpson's civil trial.
newsitem.headline: Both sides rest cases in O.J. Simpson's civil trial.

text.p: Both sides in O.J. Simpson's civil case rested on Thursday, ending the evidence phase of the trial, and the judge told jurors they would be able to start their deliberations next Thursday following closing arguments.

The last witness for the plaintiffs was FBI shoeprint expert William Bodziak, who testified that the shoes Simpson was seen wearing in 30 photographs taken at a Sept. 26, 1993, Buffalo Bills football game were uncommon Bruno Magli Lorenzo shoes.

Bodziak had previously testified that it was the distinctive sole of the Italian designer shoes that left the bloody shoeprints leading from the scene where Simpson's ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman were stabbed and slashed to death on June 12, 1994. Simpson has denied ever owning a pair of Bruno Maglis.
Bodziak testified in the criminal trial that only 299 pairs of Bruno Magli shoes, including the Lorenzo model, were sold in the United States between 1991 and 1993.

Before Bodziak took the stand in the civil trial, former FBI photo expert Gerald Richards told the jury he had examined the pictures, taken by freelance photographer E.J. Flammer, and they were authentic.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki and attorneys in the case were due to discuss jury instructions on Friday. Closing arguments were set to begin on Tuesday following Monday's Martin Luther King Day observance, when the court was to be closed.

After Daniel Petrocelli, lead attorney for the plaintiffs, said he was resting his rebuttal case, Simpson's chief defence attorney, Robert Baker, said he too was resting. Jurors, who have sat through two-and-a-half months of evidence, smiled and looked relieved.
Although the evidence was spread over a period of months, testimony from the 101 witnesses was heard in only 41 days because of holidays and weekends.

In contrast, evidence in Simpson's criminal trial, in which he was acquitted of the murders in October 1995, was spread over nine months, involving 133 days in which the jury heard from 120 witnesses. In the civil trial, he is battling a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims.

Richards previously testified that a single photograph of Simpson, taken at the same football game by a different photographer and showing him wearing what Bodziak identified as Bruno Magli Lorenzos, was genuine.
In his testimony on Thursday, Richards said of Flammer's photos, "I could find no alteration or addition in the photographs of Mr. Simpson."

Earlier on Thursday two expert witnesses attacked the defence theory that blood in the case was planted by police and the evidence was contaminated in a botched investigation. One expert said it was "absolutely ridiculous" to suggest that evidence had been contaminated, and a second said there was no evidence that blood had been planted.
Although the preservative EDTA was present in trace amounts in blood evidence, molecular biologist Terry Lee said that did not mean the blood had been planted.
Defence lawyers have claimed that blood from samples taken from Simpson and from the body of his ex-wife was planted by police to incriminate the former American football star.
